newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-DUTCH CLUBS FACE BIG DROP IN TV REVENUES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DUTCH CLUBS FACE BIG DROP IN TV REVENUES.

text.p: Dutch league soccer clubs face a steep drop in revenues from television rights to their games under a new deal between the Dutch soccer association (KNVB) and local broadcasters.

The deal, signed on Saturday, will bring about 80 million guilders ($43 million) a year into the Dutch game, ANP news agency said, compared with a previous agreement with the now-defunct Sport7 channel worth 140 million guilders annually.
Sport7 ceased transmission in December, running up losses of at least 100 million guilders in just four months of operations.

Dutch public broadcaster NOS won the coveted rights to highlights of the local premier league games, while the Holland Media Group, which runs three private channels, tied up the broadcasts of Dutch international matches until 2002.

The Dutch deal pales before the unprecedented riches TV has brought into other major European leagues. In Britain, pay television operator BSkyB paid 670 million pounds ($1.1 billion) for live rights to English premier league games until 2001.
"(The broadcasters) have profited optimally from our weak negotiating position," Jorien van den Herik, chairman of Feyenoord Rotterdam told ANP. "I would do that myself."
Live rights remain a ray of hope for the clubs.

The "big three", Feyenoord, Ajax Amsterdam and PSV Eindhoven have retained the rights to sell their home games to the highest bidder this season. The other 15 premier league clubs also want to negotiate independently from next season, the agency said.
